items.title: 2025 Infrastructure State and Condition Report, Appendix B, asset hierarchy table; IIS03137
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Integrated Infrastructure Services
items.source_date: Presented January 21, 2026; inventory as of December 31, 2024

citations.finding: The replacement-value distribution for the City-named Roads class is 70.8% Good (A&B), 16.2% Fair (C), 11.2% Poor (D&F), and 1.7% Not Rated. The class contains Paved Roads, Unpaved Roads, and Curbs. The report's inventory is as of December 31, 2024.
citations.establishes: The published Roads-class D-and-F share on the replacement-value denominator is above 10% and below 25%; under the brief's thresholds this is Partially supported.

citations.finding: The Roads class is not wholly rated poor: the table reports 70.8% Good (A&B), 16.2% Fair (C), 11.2% Poor (D&F), and 1.7% Not Rated by replacement value. The brief's generality threshold of 25% is not met.
citations.establishes: The condition distribution does not meet the primary threshold for Supported.

citations.finding: Appendix B reports Roads replacement value of C$10,484,313,206: A/B 70.8%, C 16.2%, D/F 11.2%, and not rated 1.7%. Nested rows are Paved Roads (D/F 12.5%), Unpaved Roads (100% not rated), and Curbs (D/F 7.0%).
citations.establishes: The City's published replacement-value condition distribution for its Roads class and each nested class.

citations.finding: The report states that its asset data were collected as of 2024-12-31.
citations.establishes: The date of the inventory underlying the rating.

citations.finding: The same Roads row rates 70.8% A/B and only 11.2% D/F by replacement value. The previous report rated Roads 11.4% D/F as of 2022-12-31; the published pair does not show deterioration.
citations.establishes: The failing part is the proposition's claim about the class as a whole, rather than a substantial minority.

items.title: City Council - Budget - November 30, 2022, post-meeting minutes

citations.finding: Council's adopted motion approved CM-20-0330 for $100,000,000 in the same four annual amounts, with funding coming from Tax-Supported Debt; it carried 9 to 4.
citations.establishes: The council-approved amount, schedule, stated source, and disposition.

citations.finding: Several proposals to amend CM-20-0330 were withdrawn during deliberations, and a later proposal to reduce the profile by $50 million was defeated. The record evidence consulted does not show an adopted transfer of its renewal allocation into CM-20-0330.
citations.establishes: The adopted approval did not itself establish a transfer from an identified renewal-funded profile. A transfer is distinct from whether the approved source was eligible under the brief's definition.

citations.finding: Council's December 2022 minutes record approval of the C$100 million profile funded from tax-supported debt.
citations.establishes: Council's actual approval and the funding source stated in its motion.

items.title: City of Edmonton renewal investment shortfall sits at $1.5B: report (CBC News)

citations.finding: CBC (June 2025) reported the report's shortfall as $1.5B for 2023-26. Read via search excerpt; the page returned 403. The Spring 2024 figures imply about $1.61B, so the City's dollar figure varies with the budget version used ($3.5B vs $3.6B ideal).
citations.establishes: That S is not a single fixed City number. The classification holds across the range.

items.title: Edmonton mayor wants more infrastructure funding in provincial budget (CBC News)

citations.finding: CBC reported (Feb 2026, on the infrastructure committee reports) that the City has kept the share of all its assets rated poor 'hovering around 10 per cent since 2017'. Only the search-result excerpt was read; the page returned 403.
citations.establishes: That the City's portfolio-wide poor share was reported at about 10%. This is consistent with a Roads figure near the 10% boundary, which is what keeps the verdict out of the Supported band. It is portfolio-wide, not Roads.

items.title: Infrastructure State and Condition

citations.finding: The City defines its five-point scale as A very good, B good, C fair, D poor, and F very poor; its webpage says the condition measure assesses physical condition and how it permits the asset to meet its intended service level.
citations.establishes: The meaning of the City's condition grades and the general basis of its condition assessment.
citations.quote: A-very good, B-good, C-fair, D-poor and F-very poor

items.title: 2023-2026 Capital Budget, CM-20-0330 profile sheet and Appendix A

citations.finding: The adopted CM-20-0330 profile is for $100,000,000, with annual amounts of $5,950,000 in 2023, $26,750,000 in 2024, $33,650,000 in 2025, and $33,650,000 in 2026; the profile identifies Tax-Supported Debt as the funding source.
citations.establishes: The entire approved amount and its identified funding source. The source is tax-supported debt, not a grant shown as restricted.

citations.finding: The adopted 2023-2026 Capital Budget states that ideal renewal investment was $3.58 billion and funding available to renewal was $1.95 billion, leaving a “renewal funding gap of $1.63 billion for 2023-2026.” It also says the City is funding renewal to approximately 54% of ideal investment.
citations.establishes: A City-published renewal shortfall for the same four-year capital budget cycle as the $100 million numerator.
citations.quote: the City has a renewal funding gap of $1.63 billion for 2023-2026

citations.establishes: The numerator for the comparison is an approved capital amount covering 2023-2026.

citations.finding: The City's $1.63 billion gap is much larger than $100 million: the ratio is about 6.13%, below the brief's 25% threshold for Supported. The City says the 54% overall funding rate is affected by constrained, dedicated funding, and that the unconstrained-funded part achieves approximately 31% of ideal investment.
citations.establishes: The approved amount is a real but minority share of the City's published gap and does not reach the primary serious-share threshold.

items.title: City of Edmonton 2024 Financial Annual Report, Asset Renewal Investment; Fall 2025 Supplemental Budget presentation

citations.finding: The 2024 Financial Annual Report says the 2023–2026 renewal investment shortfall is approximately C$1.52 billion. The City's later Fall 2025 budget presentation repeats a C$1.52 billion '2023–2026 Capital Budget Renewal Funding Gap' following C$110 million in supplemental renewal funding.
citations.establishes: The latest located City shortfall figure covering the same four budget years as the C$100 million approval.

citations.finding: C$100 million is only 6.58% of the later C$1.52 billion same-period gap. The latest City figure therefore affirmatively falls short of the brief's 25% serious-share threshold.
citations.establishes: The denominator for the reviewer's arithmetic and the part of the proposition that fails.

items.title: Approved Capital Budget 2019–2022, arterial renewal discussion

citations.finding: The 2019–2022 capital budget records a Council target of fewer than 10% of arterial roads in D/F condition. That target concerns arterials, not the full Roads class or the same replacement-value denominator.
citations.establishes: A narrower Council service target exists but cannot be applied as a classification of the full Roads class.

items.title: Edmonton's budget adjustment so far (Taproot Edmonton)

citations.finding: 22 Nov 2023: Coun. Principe (seconded by Coun. Rice) moved to halve the $100M. She said the aim was to minimize tax-supported debt. Administration said the cut would save $123,000 (2024), $776,000 (2025) and $1.9M (2026) in tax-supported debt. The motion was defeated; Principe, Cartmell and Hamilton were in favour.
citations.establishes: That administration's reported answer in council treated the programme as financed by tax-supported debt. This is a lead to the profile sheet and minutes, not a verdict figure.
citations.quote: to try to minimize the tax-supported debt because that's our third-largest expense

items.title: Budget deliberations continue following $100M for Edmonton Bike Plan (Taproot Edmonton)

citations.finding: Options from a $30M reduced version to $200M were discussed before council settled on $100M. The article does not name movers or give dispositions for the other options.
citations.establishes: That other amounts were discussed in December 2022. It does not establish the minutes' record of any motion to reduce.

items.title: docs: the Roads poor-condition share has not moved in five years (PR #471, edmonton-tax-viz)

citations.finding: A third-party transcription of the 2025 ISC report's Appendix B (p. 37) gives the 'Roads' D+F share as 11.2% for 2025 on a replacement value of $10,484M, and 11.4% for 2023 on $9,747M. It also gives 2025 Good 70.8% and Fair 16.2%.
citations.establishes: That a reader of the City report transcribed these figures. It does not establish them as City figures: I could not verify them against the primary PDF.
citations.quote: the methodology of this report is different from previous years

items.title: docs: cross-read of the three pro-50 road-life sections (PR #473, edmonton-tax-viz)

citations.finding: A follow-up transcription says the printed Roads figure of 11.2% combines Paved Roads at 12.5% D+F with a $2.1B curbs line at 7%. It also says the 2020 Roads row included alleys at 64% D+F.
citations.establishes: A lead to the sub-class structure of the City's Roads class. Not verified against the primary document.

citations.establishes: A lead that corroborates an S of about $1.5B. It is not itself the verdict figure.

items.title: Edmonton city council 100 million bike lanes (Global News)

citations.finding: The Dec 9, 2022 amendment ($100M) passed 9-4; Cartmell, Hamilton, Principe and Rice were opposed. The article names no funding source, and the mover is not named.
citations.establishes: Approval and vote. It does not establish the funding source, which is why U stays at $100.0M on admissible evidence.

items.title: Adopted 2023–2026 Capital Budget, CM-20-0330 profile, pp. 540–543

citations.finding: The adopted profile's funding-source table lists only tax-supported debt: C$5.950 million in 2023, C$26.750 million in 2024, C$33.650 million in 2025 and C$33.650 million in 2026, totalling C$100.000 million. The source table prints in C$ thousands. No grant terms are implicated.
citations.establishes: The identity and amount of every original funding source.

citations.finding: The adopted budget's Table 6 reports C$3,575.584 million in 'RIMS Ideal Investment' and C$1,945.673 million in 'Funded RIMS Ideal Investment' for 2023–2026, or 54.4% funded. The City calls the rounded C$1.63 billion difference its 'Renewal Funding Gap.'
citations.establishes: The original approved cycle's renewal requirement, funded amount and City's own name for their difference.

citations.finding: The City's budget distinguishes C$2,194.927 million of total funded renewal from C$1,945.673 million of the modelled ideal requirement funded in 2023–2026. It excludes early renewal work and other items when calculating the gap; using the larger funded-budget line as though it were the gap calculation would misstate the City's basis.
citations.establishes: A material distinction between total approved renewal and the portion compared with the modelled ideal.

items.title: Bylaw 20394 and report FCS01698rev

citations.finding: The borrowing bylaw subsequently authorized debt for the specified active-transportation project. It limits what may be done under that authorization; it does not show that Council could never have chosen road or alley renewal when allocating the general tax-supported debt.
citations.establishes: A later project-specific borrowing authorization and a practical constraint on redirection after approval.

items.title: Spring 2024 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment, 2023-2026 Capital Budget (City of Edmonton report)

citations.finding: The originally approved 2023-2026 Capital Budget identified ideal renewal investment of $3.5B, with funding available for renewal at only 54% of it. Once constrained programs (e.g. Neighbourhood Renewal) and bridges are set aside, the remainder was funded at about 30.7% of ideal. Read via search excerpt; direct fetch returned 403.
citations.establishes: The City's own 2023-2026 renewal requirement and funded share. The unfunded part, about $1.61B, is arithmetic on City figures.
citations.quote: ideal renewal investment was identified as $3.5 billion; however, funding available for renewal was only 54 per cent

items.title: Spring 2025 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment, Attachment 4, item 4.1-1; Bylaw 21265 report

citations.finding: Council approved a C$430,000 reduction to CM-20-0330 in June 2025 for profile 25-25-9506, Dunluce Neighbourhood and Alley Renewal; the City's bylaw report says the transferred debt funded active-transportation connections there. Its destination profile name alone does not establish road or alley surface renewal spending.
citations.establishes: The approved transfer and its stated destination, while qualifying an inference from the destination profile's name.
